# Text on an image

Put the exact words in quotes, describe the lettering, keep the text short and check every character.

Applies to: image.

## Rules

1. Put the exact words in double quotes, in the language they should appear: the poster reads "MORNING BLEND".
   - Why: Five vendors give this same advice; without quotes the model may reword or invent the text.
2. Describe the lettering in words: weight, style, size, colour and where it sits. For example bold white condensed sans-serif capitals, centered in the top third, with a thin line of small type below it.
   - Why: The Nano Banana, GPT Image and FLUX vendors all advise naming the font style.
3. Keep the text short: a headline, a name, a few words. Riftland's own ad and marketing studios do the same, with one to three strings of at most six words for text drawn inside an ad image.
   - Why: Even the families presented as strong at text list small, dense or long text among their weak points, and the FLUX vendor says to keep text short. One independent test of a recent Seedream version found a few wrong characters in a long text.
4. Say that nothing else should be written: spelled exactly as written, and no other text. Riftland's director uses the same words in the prompts it assembles.
   - Why: It stops the model from adding filler lettering around your words.
5. Spell an unusual name letter by letter, or write it in capitals, when you ask the GPT Image family for it: the name is A-U-R-E-L-I-A.
   - Applies to the families: GPT Image.
   - Why: The vendor's own cookbook suggests it for tricky words.
6. Pick a model built for text when the words are the point. Vendors present the Nano Banana, GPT Image, FLUX and Ideogram families as strong at text, and Qwen Image as strong at complex layouts, very small text and several languages. These are vendor claims: check the model's facts and the evidence marked on its card.
7. Always look at the result before using it: open it with media_view at full detail and read every character. If one word is wrong, change only that word with `change_of` and keep everything else.
   - Why: No tool in Riftland checks spelling for you.

## Do and don't

- Don't: Make a poster that says welcome to our grand opening this saturday with all our offers.
  Do: A poster with the headline "GRAND OPENING" in bold white condensed sans-serif capitals, centered in the top third, and below it the line "Saturday, 10 am" in thin type. Spelled exactly as written, and no other text.
- Don't: A sign with a long paragraph about the history of the shop.
  Do: A hand-painted shop sign reading "FIELD & FLOUR" in cream letters on dark green, weathered wood, soft morning light.

## Checklist

- [ ] Are the exact words in quotes?
- [ ] Did you describe the lettering and where it goes?
- [ ] Are there three short strings at most?
- [ ] Did you say no other text?
- [ ] Did you read every character in the result?
